Q: Bit numbering and endianness A:

First things first: these files are big-endian, not little-endian, as denoted in the docs for IFF: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interchange_File_Format (and also, as it was the native working order for the Amiga CPU).

Then, if you where looking at an actual 16bit structure stored as little endian in a byte stream (which is not the case):

You aren't saying how you are "aiming" at those bits, which programming language, etc... But most of the times, you would use a tool that reads a 16bit field as 2 bytes, and that will take care of the endianness for you, as far as you do the correct conversion steps:

So, you should never have to care if it was "bit 8" at some point (also, it would not be "bit 8": you could call it "bit 0 on the first byte of the field". Because "bit 8" onlhy applies if you read the 2 bytes as a 16bit value, and at that point, you should have read then in the correct order, and it will be at position 0.

If you are running a self-made script, or assembler snippet (you don't mention what you are doing), that goes through it byte-by-byte, is the only way that would be relevant, and then, yes, you should target "bit 0 on the low order byte, which comes on the lower memory address".

Also, if you are checking (or editing) the file contents with a byte-by-byte interactive tool which prints the contents in hexadecimal, you will see the bit in the low-order byte, of course - regardless, it should not be called "bit 8".

Q: How to access a Rstudio blogdown website on local network? A:

Try blogdown::serve_site(host = '0.0.0.0') to allow connections from outside networks (if your firewall permits). To know the differences between 127.0.0.1 and 0.0.0.0, you may see this post or this. You can also use 192.168.1.4 if you are sure this local IP won't change (sometimes it may change, e.g., after you restart the wireless router).

A word of caution: enabling others to access files on your computer may introduce security risks. Please do this only if you understand the consequences and trust the outside connections. In your case, it is probably fine (people outside of your home network shouldn't be able to visit your website served locally on your computer).

Q: Edit Control Style not applying to RichEdit in CreateWindowEx A:

The "RichEdit" control class has its own set of styles.

But ES_NUMBER is one of them, according to MSDN. However, note the comment by ElmueSoft.

To filter input to only digits without help from the control, you can subclass it. You'd need to handle quite a few messages though. WM_CHAR is the most obvious, but WM_PASTE and WM_SETTEXT can have non-numeric text passed in.

Good information on subclassing:

  • https://devblogs.microsoft.com/oldnewthing/20090507-00/?p=18333
  • https://devblogs.microsoft.com/oldnewthing/20031111-00/?p=41883

Q: Get a datetime object to specify an instant for every timezone A:

A datetime object is either naive (no specific time zone) or aware (a single specific time zone). But you can control the display with datetime.astimezone:

import datetime as dt
import zoneinfo as zi

now = dt.datetime.now(tz=dt.UTC)  # UTC Timezone
print(now)
print(now.astimezone())  # Local Timezone (Pacific Daylight for me)
print(now.astimezone(tz=zi.ZoneInfo('America/New_York')))  # Specific TZ

Output:

2026-04-20 17:05:36.538249+00:00
2026-04-20 10:05:36.538249-07:00
2026-04-20 13:05:36.538249-04:00

Q: Java ReferenceQueue and garbage collection A:

It’s not clear what kind of problem you are constructing here. The cited statement does nowhere imply that your scenario wouldn’t work. It says before a JVM would throw an OutOfMemoryError, it would first attempt to free memory by clearing soft references, which would notify your cleaner, which is exactly what you want. Of course, it would be much simpler if your softly reachable object has an ordinary reference to the associated data, so all of it would be freed automatically when the soft references are cleared, without the need to run a cleaner.

Q: What exactly does builder.Services.AddControllers() do? A:

ASP.Net Core has an inbuilt dependency injection framework. So, that means we do not need containers like the UnityContainer to inject the dependencies into our application.

Now for an Mvc Application there will be a lot of classes that needs to be injected to have the Mvc application working. These classes are all categorised and bundled inside their own extensions methods of IServiceCollection. In the code above the following are the extensions method that bundles the services to be injected for their functionality.

  • AddMvcCore()
  • AddApiExplorer()
  • AddAuthorization()
  • AddCors()
  • AddDataAnnotations()
  • AddFormatterMappings()

All these methods are chained and invoked inside the parent wrapper extension method that is AddControllersCore() which is called from the AddControllers() method.

Q: Unzip files with SQL A:

Others suggest you can use Powershell which would have been the only older native windows method for XP to early Windows 10.

But current Windows 10 and 11 have a command line unzipper in Tar.EXE. it is easy once you understand its oddities to unpack/update from local or web zip files etc. (for web.zip using curl)

Example general usage https://stackoverflow.com/a/70011759/10802527

OR say for download chrome headless shell try something like

set "download=chrome-headless-shell-win32.zip"
set "variant=win32/%download%"

curl -o LATEST_RELEASE_STABLE.txt https://googlechromelabs.github.io/chrome-for-testing/LATEST_RELEASE_STABLE
set /p version=<LATEST_RELEASE_STABLE.txt
curl -O https://storage.googleapis.com/chrome-for-testing-public/%version%/%variant%
tar -xf %download%

Usage is only limited by your ingenuity.
